section-183-5.FOR: The operational purposes specified in the warrant
section-183-5.TO: be ones specified, in a list maintained by the heads of the intelligence services (“the list of operational purposes”), as purposes which they consider are operational purposes for which material obtained under bulk equipment interference warrants may be selected for examination

section-183-6.TO: specify all of the operational purposes which, at the time the warrant is issued, are specified in the list of operational purposes

section-183-7.TO: be specified in the list of operational purposes
section-183-7.ONLY WITH: the approval of the Secretary of State

section-183-8.ONLY IF: satisfied that the operational purpose is specified in a greater level of detail than the descriptions contained in section 178(1)(b) or (2)

section-183-9.TO: give a copy of the list of operational purposes to the Intelligence and Security Committee of Parliament
section-183-9.AT: the end of each relevant three-month period

section-183-11.TO: review the list of operational purposes

section-185-1.TO: be renewed by an instrument issued by the Secretary of State
section-185-1.AT: any time during the renewal period

section-185-4.FOR: The decision to renew a bulk equipment interference warrant
section-185-4.TO: be taken personally by the Secretary of State
be signed by the Secretary of State

section-186-1.FOR: The provisions of a bulk equipment interference warrant
section-186-1.TO: be modified by an instrument issued by the person making the modification

section-186-4.FOR: a major modification adding or varying any operational purpose
section-186-4.TO: be made by the Secretary of State

section-186-4.FOR: a major modification adding or varying any operational purpose
section-186-4.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State considers that it is necessary on any of the grounds on which the Secretary of State considers the warrant to be necessary (see section 178(1)(b))

section-186-5.FOR: a major modification adding or varying any description of conduct
section-186-5.TO: be made by the Secretary of State

section-186-5.FOR: a major modification adding or varying any description of conduct
section-186-5.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State considers— (i) that the modification is necessary on any of the grounds on which the Secretary of State considers the warrant to be necessary (see section 178(1)(b)), and (ii) that the conduct authorised by the modification is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct

section-186-7.FOR: — (a) the Secretary of State, or (b) a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State

section-186-8.TO: be notified personally of a minor modification and the reasons for making it
section-186-8.WHERE: the modification is made by a senior official

section-186-9.TO: modify the warrant by removing that operational purpose
section-186-9.IF: at any time the person considers that any operational purpose specified in a warrant is no longer a purpose for which the examination of material obtained under the warrant is or may be necessary

section-186-10.FOR: The decision to modify the provisions of a warrant
section-186-10.TO: be taken personally by the person making the modification

section-186-11.FOR: an instrument making a major modification
section-186-11.TO: be signed by a senior official designated by the Secretary of State for that purpose
section-186-11.IF: it is not reasonably practicable for the instrument to be signed by the Secretary of State

section-186-12.TO: contain a statement that— (a) it is not reasonably practicable for the instrument to be signed by the Secretary of State, and (b) the Secretary of State has personally and expressly authorised the making of the modification

section-187-1.TO: review the Secretary of State's conclusions as to the following matters— (a) whether the modification is necessary on any of the grounds on which the Secretary of State considers the warrant to be necessary, and (b) in the case of a major modification adding or varying any description of conduct authorised by the warrant, whether the conduct authorised by the modification is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct
section-187-1.IN: deciding whether to approve a decision to make a major modification of a bulk equipment interference warrant

section-187-2.TO: — (a) apply the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review, and (b) consider the matters referred to in subsection (1) with a sufficient degree of care as to ensure that the Judicial Commissioner complies with the duties imposed by section 2 (general duties in relation to privacy)

section-187-3.TO: give the Secretary of State written reasons for the refusal
section-187-3.WHERE: the Judicial Commissioner refuses to approve a decision to make a major modification under section 186

section-187-4.TO: ask the Investigatory Powers Commissioner to decide whether to approve the decision to make the modification
section-187-4.WHERE: a Judicial Commissioner, other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner, refuses to approve a decision to make a major modification under section 186

section-188-2.TO: inform a Judicial Commissioner that the modification has been made

section-188-3.TO: — (a) decide whether to approve the decision to make the modification, and (b) notify the Secretary of State of the Judicial Commissioner's decision
section-188-3.BEFORE: the end of the relevant period

section-188-4.FOR: the person to whom the warrant is addressed
section-188-4.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done under the warrant by virtue of that modification stops as soon as possible
section-188-4.IF: the Judicial Commissioner refuses to approve the decision to make the modification

section-188-5.TO: authorise further interference with equipment for the purpose of enabling the person to whom the warrant is addressed to secure that anything in the process of being done under the warrant by virtue of the modification stops as soon as possible

section-189-1.FOR: The Secretary of State, or a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State
section-189-1.TO: cancel a bulk equipment interference warrant

section-189-2.FOR: the Secretary of State, or a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State
section-189-2.TO: cancel a bulk equipment interference warrant
section-189-2.IF: the person considers that any of the cancellation conditions are met in relation to the warrant

section-189-5.FOR: the person to whom a warrant was addressed
section-189-5.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done under the warrant stops as soon as possible
section-189-5.WHERE: the warrant is cancelled under this section

section-189-6.FOR: a warrant that has been cancelled under this section

section-190-1.FOR: the person to whom a bulk equipment interference warrant is addressed (“the implementing authority”)
section-190-1.TO: (in addition to acting alone) act through, or together with, such other persons as the implementing authority may require (whether under subsection (2) or otherwise) to provide the authority with assistance in giving effect to the warrant

section-190-2.TO: For the purpose of requiring any person to provide assistance in relation to a bulk equipment interference warrant, — (a) serve a copy of the warrant on any person who the implementing authority considers may be able to provide such assistance, or (b) make arrangements for the service of a copy of the warrant on any such person

section-190-3.TO: be served under subsection (2) on a person outside the United Kingdom for the purpose of requiring the person to provide such assistance in the form of conduct outside the United Kingdom

section-191-1.TO: ensure that arrangements are in force for securing— (a) that the requirements of subsections (2) and (5) are met in relation to the material obtained under the warrant, and (b) that the requirements of section 193 are met in relation to that material

section-192-1.TO: ensure that arrangements are in force for securing that— (a) any material obtained under the warrant is handed over to overseas authorities only if the requirements of subsection (2) are met, and (b) copies of any such material are given to overseas authorities only if those requirements are met

section-193-8.FOR: the person to whom the warrant is addressed
section-193-8.TO: notify the Secretary of State that the selection is being carried out
section-193-8.IN: a case where the selection of protected material for examination is authorised by subsection (5)

section-194-3.TO: have regard to the public interest in the confidentiality of items subject to legal privilege
section-194-3.IN: deciding whether to give an approval under subsection (2) in a case where subsection (1)(b)(i) applies

section-194-4.ONLY IF: — (a) the official considers that the arrangements made for the purposes of section 191 (safeguards relating to retention and disclosure of material) include specific arrangements for the handling, retention, use and destruction of items subject to legal privilege, and (b) where subsection (1)(b)(i) applies, the official considers that there are exceptional and compelling circumstances that make it necessary to authorise the use of the relevant criteria

section-194-7.TO: be selected for examination using the relevant criteria
section-194-7.ONLY IF: a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State has approved the use of those criteria

section-194-8.ONLY IF: the official considers that the targeted communications or other items of information are likely to be communications made or (as the case may be) other items of information created or held with the intention of furthering a criminal purpose

section-194-9.FOR: the person to whom a bulk equipment interference warrant is addressed
section-194-9.WHERE: an item subject to legal privilege which has been obtained under the warrant is retained following its examination, for purposes other than the destruction of the item

section-194-10.TO: — (a) direct that the item is destroyed, or (b) impose one or more conditions as to the use or retention of that item
section-194-10.UNLESS: the Commissioner considers that subsection (12) applies to the item

section-194-11.TO: impose such conditions under subsection (10)(b) as the Commissioner considers necessary for the purpose of protecting the public interest in the confidentiality of items subject to legal privilege
section-194-11.IF: the Commissioner considers that subsection (12) applies to the item

section-194-13.TO: require an affected party to make representations about how the Commissioner should exercise any function under subsection (10)
have regard to any such representations made by an affected party (whether or not as a result of a requirement imposed under paragraph (a))

section-195-5.FOR: The person to whom the warrant is addressed
section-195-5.TO: inform the Investigatory Powers Commissioner of the retention of the relevant material

section-195-6.TO: direct that the relevant material is destroyed
section-195-6.UNLESS: the Commissioner considers that subsection (8) applies to the relevant material

section-195-7.TO: impose such conditions as to the use or retention of the relevant material as the Commissioner considers necessary for the purpose of protecting the public interest in the confidentiality of confidential journalistic material or sources of journalistic information
section-195-7.IF: the Commissioner considers that subsection (8) applies to the relevant material

section-195-9.TO: require an affected party to make representations about how the Commissioner should exercise any function under subsections (6) and (7)
have regard to any such representations made by an affected party (whether or not as a result of a requirement imposed under paragraph (a))

section-195A-2.TO: inform the Investigatory Powers Commissioner that the approval has been given

section-195A-3.TO: — (a) consider whether the relevant condition is met as regards the use of the criteria for the selection of the material for examination, and (b) notify the Secretary of State of their decision

section-196-1.TO: — (a) select for examination any material obtained under a bulk equipment interference warrant, (b) know or believe that the selection of that material does not comply with a requirement imposed by section 193 or 194, and (c) deliberately select that material in breach of that requirement

section-196-3.FOR: proceedings for any offence which is an offence by virtue of this section
section-196-3.TO: be instituted— (a) in England and Wales, except by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions; (b) in Northern Ireland, except by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland
